source_evidence: Many bonds pay a fixed rate of interest throughout their term.
answer: Corporate bonds can have fixed or floating coupon rates. With a fixed coupon rate, the interest payments stay the same throughout the bond’s term, even when market interest rates change. With a floating rate, the rate is reset periodically—such as every six months—and the interest payments adjust with market interest rates. A floating rate is based on a bond index or another benchmark; for example, it may be set at a specified Treasury rate plus 1%.
